points.t: Thickened, itchy eczema on the face, scalp, neck and backs of hands in an older man, sparing the upper eyelids, behind the ears and under the chin.
Extreme sensitivity to UVB, UVA and sometimes visible light, behaving like contact allergy to an endogenous light-altered antigen; contact allergy is common alongside.
Strict photoprotection (including visible light), emollients, potent topical steroid or tacrolimus; refer for phototesting and patch testing; specialist immunosuppression.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and drug photosensitivity as mimics; erythroderma.

points: **Itchy, red, thickened, lichenified eczematous plaques** on face (forehead, cheeks, nose), scalp in bald men, ears, **back and sides of neck, V of chest, dorsal hands/forearms**.
**Sharp cut-off** at collar and wrist/cuff; **sparing** of upper eyelids, skin creases, behind/under ears, under chin, finger webs (DermNet gallery).
Can extend to covered sites and progress to **erythroderma** in severe cases.
Present year-round but worse in summer; patients may say even indoor light/fluorescent light triggers flares.
Darker skin: hyperpigmentation and lichenification more than redness.
Severe: infiltrated papules/plaques with atypical lymphocytes (actinic reticuloid) — mimics cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (Sézary syndrome).
(photobiology unit): reduced minimal erythema dose to UVB ± UVA ± visible — confirms diagnosis and guides photoprotection.
**Patch testing and photopatch testing** (Compositae mix, fragrance, sunscreen agents, plant extracts).
Biopsy: chronic spongiotic dermatitis ± atypical lymphoid infiltrate; exclude lymphoma (Sézary cells, T-cell receptor gene studies if erythrodermic).
Bloods: ANA/ENA (exclude lupus), porphyrins; HIV in younger patients with new severe photosensitivity.

cards.name: Airborne contact dermatitis (e.g. Compositae, sawdust)
cards.clue: Involves **shaded** sites too (upper eyelids, under chin, behind ears); patch tests; may coexist with CAD

cards.name: Photoallergic drug reaction
cards.clue: Temporal link to drug; resolves after stopping (persistent light reaction = CAD-like evolution)

cards.name: PMLE
cards.clue: Younger, intermittent, clears within weeks, not lichenified

cards.name: Rosacea
cards.clue: Central face, papulopustules, telangiectasia, flushing; no eczema

items.t: Erythroderma or rapidly spreading eczema: same-day dermatology.
Persistent photosensitive eczema in an older adult: refer for **phototesting and patch testing**.

pearls.t: "Eczema in an older man that is worst on the face, neck and backs of hands — and spares behind the ears" = think CAD.
Patients may be sensitised to their **own sunscreen** — choose fragrance-free, minimal-filter or physical products and ask about reactions.
Gardening is a double hit (UV + Compositae): gloves, long sleeves, avoid chrysanthemums/daisies if allergic.
Severe disease can be life-limiting (house-bound): signpost BAD leaflet and support; consider mental health.
Many improve over years with strict avoidance.
